results.description: Remove the sort/canonicalization step from o_bundle (substitute for a genuine position-information ablation — D1 has no sequence-based task; see A-D1-05). Metric here is order-invariance, not generationAccuracy, because generationAccuracy's own scoring already sorts both sides before comparing and so would not detect this change.

assumptions.claim: D1 benchmark tier uses a 10-phoneme English consonant subset (§H.3.2's tier), each represented as exactly 3 features: place, manner, voicing.
assumptions.rationale: Appendix A only worked 5 illustrative features/phonemes. A slightly larger, fixed-arity set is the minimum needed to run a real discovery/test split (H.4) rather than an illustrative one. Fixed arity 3 was chosen so a single o_bundle3 operator instance suffices — this is an implementation convenience, not a claim that all phonemes are 3-feature.
assumptions.scope: D1 dataset only; does not extend to D2+ tiers.

assumptions.claim: Voicing is represented as two mutually exclusive primitives, f.voice and f.voiceless, rather than a single binary-valued feature.
assumptions.rationale: Keeps every phoneme at fixed arity 3 (§A-D1-01) instead of variable arity 2-or-3. This is a data-modeling choice, not a phonological claim — a later phase may replace it with a true binary-valued contrast on a single primitive without invalidating discovery-set results, since it does not change which feature *distinctions* are represented, only how the voicing distinction is encoded as records.

assumptions.claim: The discovery/test split for the held-out reconstruction experiment (H.16 item 5, H.5) is: discovery = {p,b,t,d,k,m,n,f}, test = {g,v}. All of g and v's individual features (velar place, fricative manner, voice) appear somewhere in the discovery set's bundles, but the specific triples for g and v do not.
assumptions.rationale: This is the minimum split satisfying H.5's requirement (A,B,C in discovery, o(A,o(B,C)) not in discovery) with this 10-item dataset. A different split would also satisfy H.5; this one was picked, not derived, and is disclosed as such rather than presented as the only valid choice.
assumptions.scope: This experiment run only; re-randomizing the split is expected to happen once real dataset infrastructure (H.3, H.4) exists.

assumptions.claim: Bundling the held-out phonemes' known component features via o_bundle produces the correct gold structure, and the resulting derivation's content hash does not match any derivation produced during discovery — i.e. genuine unseen composition (§15's emergence definition), not lookup.
assumptions.rationale: This is the actual empirical claim under test in reconstruction.test.js — it is falsifiable: if either the structure is wrong, or (impossibly, given the engine's design, but checked anyway) the held-out hash collides with a discovery hash, the test fails and this hypothesis is logged as rejected, not silently passed.
assumptions.scope: D1 tier, this engine version only.
